text:
The leap from manager to leader is a wild ride, and it’s getting wilder. Today’s leaders face a landscape where AI isn’t just a tool; it’s a game-changer. But navigating this realm requires more than just technical know-how. 

I’ve seen firsthand how leaders are challenged to govern systems they can’t fully grasp. It’s not enough to just know how AI works; we must also understand its implications on our teams and our customers. Who are we including in our discussions? Are our teams diverse enough to reflect the society we serve? 

Morgan Stanley’s recent shift in forecasting reflects the urgency of this conversation. AI spending is soaring, but are we equipped to manage its impact responsibly? 

As I transition into the world of AI consulting, I’m constantly reminded: the human element must not be overshadowed by the technology. 

Reflect on this: How are you ensuring that your leadership adapts to the rapid changes in technology without losing sight of the people it affects?

diagram_spec.diagram_prompt: Compare traditional management vs. modern leadership in the context of AI integration and human element considerations.
